result.summary: Extracts the spender test framework out of feature_taproot.py into a shared test_framework/spenders.py module and adds a new feature_legacy_script.py functional test. The new test checks legacy script interpreter edge cases across bare, P2SH, and P2WSH scripts, and supports the --dumptests mode for populating QA script assets.
result.problem: Bitcoin Core's dumped script test assets lacked coverage for several subtle legacy script execution boundaries that alternative implementations had gotten wrong. In addition, the spender framework and test dumper logic were tied exclusively to the Taproot test, preventing other script test suites from generating test asset dumps.
evidence: PR description: 'These were discovered by finding gaps in alternate implementations (bitcoin-s and rbitcoin)'
Commit d7e3279392: 'None of the current script assets catch an interpreter that gets these wrong.'
result.scope_notes: Commit 1 is a large mechanical refactor (~800 lines moved from test/functional/feature_taproot.py into test/functional/test_framework/spenders.py).
result.changed_since_previous: Instead of adding legacy script spenders directly to feature_taproot.py, the spender framework and runner have been extracted into a reusable test_framework/spenders.py mixin and module, and the new spenders are placed in a dedicated feature_legacy_script.py test.
result.card: Extracts the spender testing and test-vector dumping framework from feature_taproot.py into a shared test framework mixin and introduces feature_legacy_script.py. The new functional test covers legacy script interpreter edge cases (such as OP_CHECKSEQUENCEVERIFY with -2, 5-byte numeric inputs, OP_IFDUP with negative or non-minimal zero, OP_ROLL with duplicate stack values, OP_16 in P2SH scriptSigs, and P2SH 1,000-element stack boundaries). These test gaps were identified from differences across alternative Bitcoin implementations like bitcoin-s and rbitcoin. Merging this enables generating updated script test vectors for bitcoin-core/qa-assets#297.

risk.why: Touches only functional test infrastructure and test scripts; a bug could only cause functional test failures in CI.
